keyVerseText: These things said he: and after that he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
rootMeaning: The word ἐξυπνίζω (exypnízō) derives from the root ἔξυπνος (éxypnos), which literally means "out of sleep" or "awake." This etymology emphasizes a transition from a state of sleep to wakefulness, highlighting not just the act of waking but the movement outward from sleep itself. This root sense enriches the common English gloss "to awaken" by underscoring the dynamic process of emerging from unconsciousness into alertness.
usageInScripture: The term ἐξυπνίζω appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in John 11:11, where it is translated as "I may awake." This singular usage shows a consistent meaning focused on rousing someone from sleep. Its limited occurrence suggests that the word carries a precise and deliberate nuance rather than a broad or varied semantic range, reinforcing the idea of intentional awakening.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding ἐξυπνίζω in its original sense as "awakening out of sleep" invites believers to consider spiritual awakening as a vital theme in Scripture. Sleep often symbolizes death or spiritual dormancy, so this verb points to the power of Christ to bring life and consciousness where there was previously unconsciousness or death. It reminds Christians that faith involves not just passive existence but an active rousing by God’s initiative. This awakening is foundational to the gospel message, where Christ calls believers from death to life, from slumber to spiritual alertness.
keyVerseReflection: In John 11:11, Jesus says, "Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep." Here, ἐξυπνίζω conveys Jesus’ intentional purpose to rouse Lazarus, who is metaphorically described as sleeping, from death. The word highlights the hope and power in Christ’s coming—that He does not merely observe death but actively awakens and restores life. This usage deepens the understanding of Jesus as the one who conquers death by awakening those who are in their final sleep.
